subject.title: AI safety taxonomy: plugin-emitted detectors and evals

question: Should external plugins be allowed to emit canonical AI-safety taxonomy events, and what manifest authorization, provenance, privacy, and schema-version guarantees must the public Plugin SDK enforce?
rationale: Current main deliberately separates internal diagnostics from plugin-namespaced public events, so allowing external code to make canonical security assertions is a permanent public trust-boundary decision that automation cannot choose.

options.title: Authorize declared events
options.body: Allow external plugins to emit only declared, schema-valid event types while always preserving untrusted emitter provenance and bounded privacy-safe fields.

options.title: Reserve canonical events
options.body: Limit canonical AI-safety events to core or bundled trusted emitters and keep external plugin output on namespaced generic event streams.

options.title: Defer the public contract
options.body: Keep current event surfaces unchanged until the parent schema, exporter behavior, and privacy model are approved together.

recommendation.title: Authorize declared events
recommendation.body: Allow external plugins to emit only declared, schema-valid event types while always preserving untrusted emitter provenance and bounded privacy-safe fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal covers Plugin API boundaries, plugin ownership moves, and repository product-scope policy.
